title: Successive lower truncations have a single cohomology sheaf as cone
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with standard truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. For every integer $n$, put $E_n=\tau_{\geq -n}E$ and $E_{n-1}=\tau_{\geq -n+1}E$. Then there is a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category] $H^{-n}(E)[n]\longrightarrow E_n\longrightarrow E_{n-1}\longrightarrow H^{-n}(E)[n+1]$, where $H^{-n}(E)[n]$ denotes the complex with $H^{-n}(E)$ in degree $-n$ and zero elsewhere, and the middle map is the canonical transition map of the truncation tower.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), truncation triangle H^{-n}(E)[n] -> E_n -> E_{n-1}

proof.text: Choose a cochain-complex representative K of E. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], for each m the truncation \tau_{\ge m}E is represented by the quotient complex K/\tau_{\le m-1}K, and the transition \tau_{\ge m}E\to\tau_{\ge m+1}E by the quotient map K/\tau_{\le m-1}K\to K/\tau_{\le m}K. Elementary (Stacks Tag 08J5, the factorization of K\to\tau_{\ge a+1}K through a quasi-isomorphism K/\tau_{\le a}K\to\tau_{\ge a+1}K): the evident surjection K/\tau_{\le m-1}K\to\tau_{\ge m}K (zero in degree m-1, K^m\to K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1}) in degree m, the identity above) has degreewise kernel the two-term complex K^{m-1}/\ker(d^{m-1})\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1}), which is acyclic, so it is a quasi-isomorphism; and these quasi-isomorphisms for m=-n and m=-n+1 commute with the quotient maps K/\tau_{\le -n-1}K\to K/\tau_{\le -n}K and q_{-n}. Hence E_n and E_{n-1} are represented by the canonical complexes \tau_{\ge -n}K and \tau_{\ge -n+1}K, and the canonical transition is represented by the quotient map q_{-n}:\tau_{\ge -n}K\to\tau_{\ge -n+1}K. Applying [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-ses] with m=-n gives a degreewise short exact sequence 0\to C_{-n}(K)\to\tau_{\ge -n}K\to\tau_{\ge -n+1}K\to0, together with a quasi-isomorphism H^{-n}(K)[n]\to C_{-n}(K). The latter complex represents H^{-n}(E)[n].

Applying [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the short exact sequence from Step 1 gives a distinguished triangle C_{-n}(K)\to E_n\to E_{n-1}\to C_{-n}(K)[1] in the derived category; the second arrow is the canonical transition because it is induced by q_{-n}.

The quasi-isomorphism H^{-n}(K)[n]\to C_{-n}(K) becomes an isomorphism in D(\mathcal A) by the definition of the derived category. Transporting the distinguished triangle of Step 2 across this isomorphism, using (TR1) that a triangle isomorphic to a distinguished triangle is distinguished, yields H^{-n}(E)[n]\to E_n\to E_{n-1}\to H^{-n}(E)[n+1]. Naturality follows from the naturality asserted in [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-ses] and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle].
